title: Audit Console through computer use and design a focused multi-screen workspace
description: Real owner feedback: excessive scrolling, everything on one page feels like a generic Bootstrap layout. Clean, clear and functional first. Session Manager must assign existing owner-console web UI specialist. Inspect actual live installed Console http://127.0.0.1:4174/console with computer use, not source-only review. Cover every navigation area, nested operational panels and action flows; read-only on live, explore writes only in isolated demo. Actually view screenshot evidence desktop and mobile, keyboard navigation, navigation position/history, refresh/draft retention, density, scrolling and empty/failure/loading states. Document visited screens and concrete issues with screenshot references. Propose focused routes/views, compact overview, contextual drilldowns and per-agent conversations, conditional pipelines, accessible navigation and honest runtime/approval status. Retain dark mode/TORCH mark. Audit and proposal only; do not rewrite UI before review. Use applicable frontend/browser skills and disclose computer-use capability blockers instead of claiming completion.
acceptanceCriteria: Session Manager assigns the existing web UI identity through revisioned backlog transitions
Actual browser/computer-use navigation and inspected screenshots cover every current area with URL, viewport and interaction notes
Live project state is not mutated during the audit; interactive mutation flows use isolated demo
Prioritized usability findings trace to observed screens, not generic recommendations
Information architecture proposes genuinely separate focused views, not anchor links on another long page
Desktop/mobile and keyboard/refresh/draft behavior are covered; branding and permission gates preserved
Report defines measurable implementation acceptance criteria; no implementation or release is implied
